accuracy.title: How well does Maskera find personal data?
accuracy.lede: What matters most is how little personal data stays in plain text. Here are our current numbers, a plain comparison with other models that support Swedish, and what to keep in mind.
accuracy.currentBody: Published Maskera v20 (43 MB), measured on Swedish test sets on 2026-11-25.
accuracy.comparisonTitle: Compared with other models that support Swedish
accuracy.comparisonBody: We only compare models that actively support Swedish. All three ran on the same 121 Swedish texts with 211 names, places and organisations, both with normal casing and all lowercase (like a quick chat message).

accuracy.comparisonSummary: Maskera caught all 211 names, places and organisations in both runs despite being 7 to 11 times smaller. KBLab edged ahead slightly on exact category label in normal text (89.4% vs 88.2%); in lowercase Maskera led clearly (87.4% vs 83.2% and 62.1%).
accuracy.contextBody: Personal identity numbers are easy to catch with rules. The hard part in Swedish is words that can be either a person's name or an everyday word or diagnosis.

limits: The test texts were written by Maskera's developer. They show direction and catch regressions between releases, but they are not an independent benchmark across all Swedish text.

No automatic masking is 100% error-free. Unusual names or noisy scans can slip through, so always review the text yourself when a mistake would carry high impact.

security.metaTitle: security: network requests and model integrity · maskera
security.metaDescription: Maskera's security boundaries, network requests, pinned model artefacts, safe restoration and private vulnerability reporting.
security.title: Security in maskera
security.lede: All masking runs locally on your device. Here is how data moves, how model files are verified and how to report a vulnerability.
dataFlow: Your text and restoration key are never sent to Maskera. The rule layer has no network dependencies and the AI model runs locally in the browser or your own Node process.
On first use, the npm package downloads the AI model (43 MB) once as a regular static file and caches it locally. You can also host the model files on your own server with no external requests.
artifacts: Every npm release is pinned to an exact model version on Hugging Face, so weights cannot change quietly without a new package release.
The build checks every model file with SHA-256. An unexpected or corrupted file stops the build instead of being used silently.
restore: The key contains the original values and must be treated as personal data. Do not log it or store it beside the masked text.

restore() inserts real values wherever placeholder tokens occur. Do not restore untrusted output that will then be fetched as a URL, rendered as HTML or written to logs. Masking protects what is sent; restoration does not sanitise what comes back.
A placeholder already present in the input is never allocated again. Planting [PERSONNUMMER_1] in the source text therefore cannot capture a real value.
security.scopeIntro: Report privately if you find, for example:
inScope: original values or the restoration key leaking to the network, storage or logs contrary to the documented local processing
unexpected network requests beyond the documented one-time downloads of the model and runtime
XSS or injection in the demo at maskera.dev
an exploitable supply-chain risk in the npm packages or model artefacts
an intentional construction that hides personal data from the detectors while a person or language model can still read it
security.qualityBody: A model missing an unusual name or a rule lacking an edge case is normally a quality issue, not a vulnerability. Report such examples publicly so they can become regression cases. A reproducible intentional bypass, however, belongs in a private security report.
security.reportBody: Do not open a public issue for a possible security flaw. Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting. Only the latest published versions of maskera and @maskera/core receive security fixes, so update before reporting.
security.productionBody: The production guide covers secure integration, fallback to rules, logging, self-hosting, domain-specific test corpora and the production checklist. Maskera is a data-minimisation layer, not a guarantee of compliance or complete detection.
security.extensionBody: This page covers the npm packages and open demo. The browser extension's local data handling and licence model are documented in the customer portal.

transparency.metaTitle: privacy & transparency: what leaves the device · maskera
transparency.metaDescription: See what Maskera does, what leaves the device, how the Swedish AI model was trained and which personal data it can miss.
transparency.title: Privacy & transparency
transparency.lede: See what Maskera does, what leaves the device, how the model was trained and what it can miss.
how: Maskera reads the text and replaces detected personal data with placeholders such as [NAMN_1] or [PERSONNUMMER_1]. The AI service sees the placeholders. Afterwards, you can restore the originals locally.

Two layers work together. Rules find fixed-format data such as Swedish personal identity numbers, phone numbers and email addresses. A small Swedish AI model finds names, places, organisations and addresses in running text.
The model runs directly in the browser or in your own Node process. The text therefore does not need to be sent to an external service for analysis.
data: All masking runs locally on your device (browser, extension or your own Node process). Text and restoration keys are never sent to Maskera.
Vercel Analytics counts page views anonymously without cookies, and Vercel handles technical request data for hosting. Text entered in the tool is never included.
The rule layer has no network dependencies. The npm package downloads the model and runtime once as static files and can be self-hosted (details on the security page).
limits: Maskera is evaluated openly. The figures, method and caveats are available on the accuracy page.
Known weak points include table-like dumps, OCR noise and data written as words, such as ‘zero seven zero’. Capital letters, misspellings and messy number formats are, however, included in the tests.
Masking is an additional protection layer, not a guarantee. Names and places are found probabilistically and can be missed. Keep other controls in place when an error could have serious consequences.
Maskera supports data minimisation but does not guarantee regulatory compliance. The organisation using the tool remains the data controller.

items.body: Vercel Analytics counts page views using anonymous, cookieless statistics without profiling. The statistics never contain text entered in the tool.

items.title: Hosting

items.title: Text entered in the tool

agentSetup.promptTitle: Let your agent set up Maskera for you
agentSetup.promptDescription: Paste this prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop, OpenCode or any other agent. It reads maskera.dev/llms.txt and configures the right local mode.
agentSetup.skillLabel: Or install as an agent skill:
agentSetup.promptText: Read https://maskera.dev/llms.txt and help me connect Maskera (@maskera/mcp) locally in my setup (local LLM proxy for enforced redaction across any agent, or MCP server for local files) so Swedish personal data never leaves my machine.

modes.label: Local proxy (any agent)
modes.summary: Strongest guarantee across any harness: sits locally in front of Anthropic and OpenAI, redacts every outgoing prompt and tool result, and restores streaming responses automatically.
modes.code:
# 1. Start the local proxy on 127.0.0.1:8787
npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy

# 2. Point any agent at the proxy:
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787 claude
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1 codex

modes.label: MCP server (files)
modes.summary: For Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex and T3 Code: maskera_read_file masks local files before the model sees them, and maskera_write_file restores answers directly to disk.

modes.label: Guard (hooks & pipes)
modes.summary: Block prompts or hook payloads containing personal data (exit code 2, prints counts and types only, never raw values) or redact text directly in a Unix pipeline.
modes.code:
# Block PII in agent hooks (exits 2 on match):
npx -y @maskera/mcp guard

# Redact a local file through a pipe:
cat document.txt | npx -y @maskera/mcp guard --redact

about.metaDescription: About Maskera: what the tool does, who is behind it (Hägvall Labs AB in Stockholm) and how to reach us at hej@maskera.dev.
about.title: About Maskera
about.lede: Maskera hides Swedish personal data locally before text reaches an AI service, log or analytics.
what: Maskera combines fixed rules (for Swedish personal identity numbers, phone numbers, emails and IBANs) with a custom-trained 43 MB Swedish AI model that finds names, places, organisations and addresses in free text.
Everything can be restored in the AI's reply using a local key that never leaves your device.
use: Browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Safari coming later) in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot and more. Free for everyday needs (rules + 20 AI/month); Pro costs SEK 149/user/month incl. VAT after 7 days free, with shared protected words and central deployment via app.maskera.dev.

AI agents (@maskera/mcp, MIT open source): local LLM proxy for Anthropic/OpenAI that masks all outgoing traffic and restores streaming replies across any harness, MCP server for masked file access, and guard for hooks.
Own code: the maskera and @maskera/core npm packages under the MIT licence, plus the maskera-sv-ner model on Hugging Face.
about.who: Maskera is developed and operated by Hägvall Labs AB (Swedish company reg. no. 559598-0110), a Swedish limited company in Stockholm founded by Joel Hägvall. The company is the data controller for maskera.dev; how the website itself processes data is described in the privacy policy. The source code, training pipeline and benchmarks are public on GitHub so the results can be reviewed and reproduced.
